newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks tax incentives for DC economy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks tax incentives for DC economy.

text.p: President Clinton Thursday called for creating an economic development corporation to provide grants and tax incentives to spur growth in financially strapped District of Columbia.
The proposed authority was described in Clinton's fiscal 1998 budget plan released today.
It is part of a broad financial aid package for D.C. proposed recently by Clinton and outlined again in today's budget.

The new Economic Development Corporation would "craft a strategic development plan" for D.C. and recommend how to use different financial incentives the federal government would provide, according to budget documents.
"It would build local economic markets, develop strategies to link District residents to newly-created jobs, and help the District foster regional economic strategies," the documents stated.
